pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Urine darkening to a port-wine hue upon light/air exposure due to porphobilinogen oxidation, alongside catastrophic neurovisceral decompensation directly triggered by cytochrome P450-inducing agents (fasting/ketosis, TMP-SMX, and fatally worsened by fosphenytoin). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder resulting from a partial deficiency of porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD / HMBS). Triggers that demand increased hepatic heme synthesis (fasting/starvation, sulfonamides, and potent CYP450 inducers like phenytoin) hyper-induce the rate-limiting enzyme delta-aminolevulinic acid synthase 1 (ALAS1). Because of the PBGD enzymatic bottleneck, non-metabolized upstream precursors—specifically delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG)—accumulate to massive, neurotoxic levels. This neurotoxicity manifests as a triad of severe autonomic instability (tachycardia, hypertension, abdominal pain without peritonitis), SIADH causing profound hyponatremia, central neuropsychiatric disturbances (psychosis, seizures), and a life-threatening, motor-predominant axonal neuropathy. Administering CYP-inducing antiepileptics like phenytoin accelerates ALAS1 activity, precipitating respiratory arrest and flaccid quadriplegia.
